instruction: Use the L-shaped tool to pull the cube towards the robot, then let go of the tool and move the hand away.

outcome.real_measurement: Pulled in (E27 term, unchanged): the cube's horizontal distance to the robot base <= 0.6 m at every judged step (ManiSkill's threshold). Real world: tracked cube pose and the base position.
Rests flat (E27 term, unchanged): smallest angle of the cube's axes to vertical <= 10 deg at every judged step.
On the table: lowest bounding-box corner within 5 mm of the table top at every judged step. Real world: RGB-D pose vs table plane.
Moved by the tool (process, new): the L-shaped tool touched the cube at some step of the episode. Real world: side camera / tool-cube contact.
Not by hand (process, new): the robot itself never touched the cube (substep-accumulated robot-cube impulse over the whole episode = 0). Real world: wrist / gripper camera.

Commanded vs actual opening (v3.2, E24c fix 3): for every arm whose gripper is within 3 cm of a judged object, measured opening minus the free-space opening of its current gripper command <= 5 mm at every judged step (a gripper still closing on, or propped open by, something fails). Real world: gripper encoder vs command.

Consequence test after the judged window (protocol v3.1/v3.2): every arm whose gripper is within 3 cm of the tool or the cube retracts its TCP 3 cm along its approach axis in 0.5 s with its last gripper command unchanged, then holds 0.5 s; the tool or the cube must move <= 1 cm. Real world: same motion, tracked pose.
Settled: the fastest bounding-box corner of every judged object moves <= 2 cm/s at every judged step, speed from positions (v3.2, E24c fix 1). Real world: frame differencing of the tracked pose.
Stays put: the cube centre moves <= 2 mm over the judged window. Real world: tracked pose, 1 s.
Stays put: the tool centre moves <= 2 mm over the judged window. Real world: tracked pose, 1 s.

counterexamples.name: expert
counterexamples.description: positive control: E27's port of ManiSkill's solution (grasp the handle, lift, hook behind the cube, pull 35 cm), then open and retreat 8 cm up

counterexamples.name: hold_tool
counterexamples.description: the pull, gripper stays closed on the tool

counterexamples.name: cage_tool
counterexamples.description: the pull, gripper opened only ~1.5 mm beyond the handle width

counterexamples.name: pull_short
counterexamples.description: the pull stops with the cube ~0.65 m from the robot base, released, retreat

counterexamples.name: pull_by_gripper
counterexamples.description: the tool is not used: the closed gripper reaches behind the cube and drags it to 0.5 m from the base

counterexamples.name: no_op
counterexamples.description: the arm stays at its start pose

source.protocol: v3 (veritask, unchanged) + imsim v3.2 signals (imsim/imsim/verify/v32.py): position-based speeds, all-link enclosure, retreat aftermath, commanded vs actual opening, 5 s settle cap
source.released_code_predicate: cube within 0.6 m (xy) of the robot base, one step (no release, no settling, no check that the tool was used)
source.reference: E27 frozen protocol-v2 contract research/results/e27_unbundle/contracts/pull_cube_tool_v2.json (sha256 426d9a0d441ef2c3093c37f1764a367a047d6cd2fa89db2f3670c2dcafb92840, prereg.json): its end-state geometry terms and thresholds are kept unchanged here; it does not run unchanged in imsim's verify layer (protocol v3: check_contract_v3 rejects it -- no release block with contact + enclosure signals, its release rule lives in E27's v2 binding; no settle block; no counterexample list), so its release (5 mm finger gap), 1 s replay settle and TCP-distance 'retreated' term are replaced by the v3.2 machinery: release by contact + all-link enclosure, commanded-vs-actual opening, retreat aftermath (consequence test), hold A + quiescence + 1 s window in a 5 s cap, position-based speeds.

notes: Tool bounding box from its collision shapes (handle + hook). Release, commanded opening and retreat over the tool and the cube; the two process terms state the task's tool use.
